result.title: Sightline: Long-Window Speculative Decoding for Fast SVG Generation
result.summary: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) generation models write a graphic as code with one forward pass per token, so drawing is slow. Speculative decoding speeds them up losslessly, and block drafters guess many tokens per pass. On SVG, many of their rounds accept the whole draft and end only at the verification window. We find that their misses are rare and clumped, and that they stay accurate far deeper into a block than on natural language. A run-length identity and three propositions show that a longer window pays once the candidates are wide, up to the drafter's horizon. We propose Sightline, which pairs a window as long as the drafter's horizon with a draft tree wide enough to fill it. Experiments cover text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG with three models on six benchmarks from MMSVG, MMSVG-2M and SArena. In every setting, Sightline is the fastest of the compared lossless decoders. On SArena, it stays the fastest when every decoder shares one loop control. It also leads in almost every setting of six models from four other families, which write SVG code, compressed SVG tokens or Lottie JSON. Analyses trace the lead to rounds that shorter windows cut off, both in loop-free content and in loops. Speculative decoding also saves time for choosing samples by rendering, which beats choosing by likelihood. These results suggest that speculative decoding on vector graphics should verify as far as the drafter sees. Code and data are available at https://github.com/LiZaiyuan0619/Sightline.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 SVG 代码生成这类逐 token 自回归绘图速度慢的问题，提出 Sightline：将草稿验证窗口拉长到 drafter 的预测视界，并用足够宽的草稿树填满该窗口，在多个文本/图像到 SVG 基准上取得最快的无损解码速度，并分析收益来自被短窗口截断的验证轮次。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「草稿—验证窗口—接受长度」的计算分配与停止判据，可能为 LVR 中并行/多 token 推理状态生成及验证式停止决策提供核查线索，但研究对象是输出解码加速而非 latent 推理状态本身。
